chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Before Sinatra and Crosby: Buck and Bubbles came first
summary: He says they played the Paramount before Sinatra, Crosby and Burns and Allen, yet earned little.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: During those performances you must have been introduced to a lot of the greats -- fantastic performers of those days. You mentioned Frank Sinatra, that you had been in contact with -- I don't know if this early in your career --

Listen, well before Frank Sinatra, before Bing Crosby, before all these guys, we were before all of them. They've been introduced to us to the extent that they've got to come to where we were. We're not going to where they were because they were

nowhere. We were in the Paramount before they ever went there. Before. All the theaters in New York we played. If you follow what I'm trying to say. Bing Crosby, Burns and Allen, Frank Sinatra were nothing compared to Buck and Bubbles when we were on the stage. No don't talk about the performers now. We're talking about being in the business. We were in the business. What good was it being in the business, getting a quarter -- lousey -- to think about it is disgraceful. Disgraceful. This is just as bad as Carter trying to talk about human rights today.
